name: Standard Ebooks
license: Public domain in the USA; Standard Ebooks editions dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0
reason: Carefully proofread public-domain editions; each repository's LICENSE.md is checked during import.
attribution: Quotations extracted from Standard Ebooks source repositories (github.com/standardebooks).

name: Project Gutenberg (via the GITenberg mirror)
license: Public domain in the USA (per Project Gutenberg catalogue rights statement)
reason: Only texts whose Project Gutenberg rights metadata is “Public domain in the USA.” are mined; licence boilerplate is stripped.
attribution: Quotations extracted from Project Gutenberg eBook texts, retrieved from the GITenberg mirror (github.com/GITenberg). Project Gutenberg is a registered trademark; this app is not affiliated with it.

name: JohsEnevoldsen/literature-clock (literature-clock.jenevoldsen.com)
reason: Non-commercial, share-alike compilation of reader-submitted excerpts (originally The Guardian’s 2011 call-out), most from in-copyright modern books. The CC licence covers the compilation, not the quoted works, so it cannot grant redistribution rights for the excerpts.

name: kapoorankush/litclock
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (quote database; software is MIT)
reason: The repository states explicitly that its MIT licence does not cover the quote database, which is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and derived from the JohsEnevoldsen corpus, cdmoro/literature-clock and the Guardian thread; most excerpts are from in-copyright books.

name: itsfoss/literary-clock
license: MIT for code; quotes taken from kapoorankush/litclock (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
reason: Its README states the quote database is taken from kapoorankush/litclock, so the same restrictions apply; the MIT software licence does not extend to the quotations.
